Name: Platform Security
Why: A review that finds the baseline absent measures the gap; it does not close it. No configuration standard exists, so nothing is established or applied.
What would move it: 2 when the baseline standard (AWS-15) is approved; 3 after two evidenced quarterly assessments (AWS-17).

Name: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
Why: The network is now documented as exposed (CF-01, CF-12); documentation of a hole is not protection.
What would move it: 2 when a security-group and VPC baseline is approved and SSH is closed; 3 with review records.

Name: Continuous Monitoring
Why: Config and Security Hub have run for 11 days in two regions of one account, routed to nobody. A prerequisite is not a score.
What would move it: 2 when monitoring is organisation-wide with a named owner and runbook (AWS-10); 3 after 90 days of handled-alert records.

Name: Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control
Why: Root MFA (1.4) and no root keys (1.3) are evidenced, but phishable MFA on admins and a live contractor login contradict the policy. A 2 already means approved but unevidenced.
What would move it: 3 when federation, FIDO2 for admins and the first quarterly review are evidenced (AWS-12, REC-02).

Name: Data Security
Why: Encryption exists at the provider level only, and Restricted data was found outside approved systems. Consistent with 2, not 3.
What would move it: 3 when customer-managed keys protect the Restricted buckets and discovery has run (AWS-11, CF-03).

Name: Asset Management
Why: This review listed accounts, regions, buckets and hosts. A cloud resource list is an input to REC-05, not an asset inventory.
What would move it: 2 when REC-05 delivers the inventory with owners and classification.

Name: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
Why: The CUECs are now evidenced as not performed, but the programme that found them is unchanged.
